title: Skyscraper functor for modules on a ringed space
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space (a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O_X$ on its site of opens), and $x\in X$, with stalk ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. For an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $M$, define $i_{x,*}M$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] by $(i_{x,*}M)(U)=M$ if $x\in U$, and $0$ otherwise. Sections are equivalently functions from the proposition $x\in U$ to $M$; restrictions are precomposition with the inclusion of membership proofs. A scalar $a\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ acts by its germ at $x$ whenever $x\in U$. Module morphisms act pointwise on sections. This defines an additive functor, extended termwise to cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules].

proof.text: Restriction is semilinear: evaluate at membership in the smaller open and use TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply' to identify the two germs.

Apply TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafUniqueGluing. For each membership proof in the union, choose an index whose open contains x and take that section value. Pairwise compatibility on intersections proves each restriction equation. Any other gluing has the same value by its restriction to the chosen member. If x is absent from the union, the section domain is empty, including for an empty cover.

The induced module maps act pointwise. Extensionality and definitional equality prove identity, composition, and additivity. The resulting functor can be extended termwise by Functor.mapHomologicalComplex.

proof_origin.place: Tag 009A (4); existing Lean docstring arguments, implemented using Mathlib germ restriction and unique gluing
